persona: Independent simulated beginner, first introduction to RILL, interested in a short melodic instrumental.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Visible MIDI, pencil and duplicate hints supported completion with only mouse input. Custom naming required many onscreen key clicks.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: Cohesive dark layout, teal waveforms and readable MIDI previews. The toolbar was dense and native white dialogs looked separate.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Drawing, duplication and trimming reacted promptly. WAV export took a noticeable interval; laboratory elapsed time is not a benchmark.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Mode-specific hints clarified editing gestures. Naming required finding Keyboard after Rename, and the WAV file dialog briefly appeared blank before rendering.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: All features required for this narrow task were visibly usable: audio, MIDI, VST assignment, mouse-only naming, project saving and WAV/MIDI exports. Broader features were not evaluated.

findings.observation: Following Double-click for MIDI opened the device library; Assign instrument created a pattern and a track visibly assigned to Rill Lab Sine.
The pencil hint said Drag to set length. Sixteen mouse-drawn notes formed a four-bar melodic phrase; drawing beyond the initial one-bar boundary extended the clip.
After Play, the playhead advanced to 003.04.49 and both audio and instrument track meters were active. No audio was auditioned.
Duplicate's visible hint described clicking a clip. Repeating both tracks and trimming their final edges to the seconds ruler produced a visible arrangement duration of 0:30.000.
File > Rename project exposed a Keyboard button. Its onscreen keys allowed the chosen title soft circuit using only mouse clicks, and the save dialog inherited that title.
Entering the custom title required an individual mouse click for each character plus Clear, Done and Apply name. It worked but was a longer interaction than the clip-editing steps.
The first WAV save-dialog capture showed a black rectangle. A subsequent screenshot showed the normal native file picker without further corrective input.
WAV options showed a 30-second arrangement and effect-tail checkbox. With tails disabled, the export displayed a progress notice then an Exported success notice. MIDI export also displayed Exported.

outcome.status: Completed through the visible UI: named arrangement, project saved, WAV and MIDI success notices seen. File contents await independent coordinator verification.
outcome.composition: Supplied Circuit rhythm audio duplicated across fourteen bars at 112 BPM. A mouse-drawn sixteen-note rising/falling melody through Rill Lab Sine was repeated alongside it. Both final clips were trimmed at 30 seconds.
outcome.playback_observed: Playhead advanced from the start to 003.04.49 and both track meters were active. Playback was stopped with the visible Stop button. This is visual evidence only, not heard audio.

limitations: No file contents or heard audio claim; independent coordinator verification follows.
Actual exported duration, PCM quality and MIDI correctness were not inspected; 30.000 seconds is the visible arrangement duration.
Software graphics and timer-paced virtual audio backend limit performance conclusions; elapsed time includes tool and screenshot overhead.
Only the laboratory Rill Lab Sine VST3 was evaluated; the initial audio was supplied.
The transient black file dialog may reflect native rendering or laboratory conditions; its underlying cause was not investigated.
